Bebai
bē'bī
n. (the head of a family of six hundred twenty and three who returned with Zerubbabel, whose house appears again with Ezra and at the sealing of the covenant)
From Hebrew Bebay, of uncertain derivation, most likely a Babylonian or Persian name taken up during the exile — as several of the family names in the register appear to be. That is itself a small witness to where these households had been living.

Biblical Definition

Bebai is one of the middling houses of the return, and the register is exact about it: “The children of Bebai, six hundred twenty and three” (Ezr 2:11). Nehemiah's copy gives six hundred twenty and eight, one of the small divergences between the two rolls that a forger harmonising his documents would have removed and a faithful copyist of two separate registers would not. A second company came up with Ezra: “And of the sons of Bebai; Zechariah the son of Bebai, and with him twenty and eight males” (Ezr 8:11). Four men of the house are listed among those who had married strange wives (Ezr 10:28), and the head of the family sealed Nehemiah's covenant (Neh 10:15). That is the whole record: a name, two counts, a small second migration, a sin confessed, and a signature. It is the ordinary shape of a Christian household in any century — numbered, mixed, repentant, and bound by covenant to the God of its fathers.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no article for Bebai; in sacred history he is the head of a family of the return from Babylon.

BEBAI, n. A proper name; the head of a family of the children of Israel.

Six hundred twenty and three of his children returned with Zerubbabel.

The parallel register in Nehemiah reckons six hundred twenty and eight.

Twenty and eight males of the house came up afterward with Ezra.

Bebai is named among those that sealed the covenant in the days of Nehemiah.

Key Scripture

Ezr 2:11 — "The children of Bebai, six hundred twenty and three."

Neh 7:16 — "The children of Bebai, six hundred twenty and eight."

Ezr 8:11 — "And of the sons of Bebai; Zechariah the son of Bebai, and with him twenty and eight males."

Neh 10:15 — "Bunni, Azgad, Bebai,"

Modern Corruption

The small numerical differences between the registers in Ezra 2 and Nehemiah 7 are offered as proof that Scripture contains errors. They are what two genuine documents of two different dates look like, and inerrancy has never meant that a copyist's numeral cannot slip.

expand to see more

The two rolls of the returned agree in most figures and differ in perhaps eighteen, and the difference is regularly produced as a straightforward contradiction. Two answers are worth stating plainly, and neither is special pleading. First, the lists are not the same document: Ezra 2 registers those who set out or were enrolled at one point, Nehemiah 7 reproduces a register he found (Neh 7:5) at a later date, after decades in which families had died out, arrived late, or been reckoned differently — and the totals in both are stated as the same grand figure, which shows the compilers were aware of their own arithmetic. Second, the doctrine of inerrancy has always been confessed of the original autographs, and the transmission of Hebrew numerals is precisely the class of detail most liable to a scribe's slip.

What must not be conceded is the inference the objection is built to carry — that because a numeral may vary, the Bible is a merely human book to be sifted for what a reader finds credible. The Scriptures are God-breathed, “All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness” (2Ti 3:16), and the Lord Himself rested an argument on a single word of a psalm and said “the scripture cannot be broken” (Joh 10:35). Six hundred twenty and three, or eight: either way, God knew which of Bebai's children went home.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Bebay (H893), Bebai; ben (H1121), son, child, in the idiom ‘the children of’; golah (H1473), the exile community; 'alah (H5927), to go up, the technical verb of the return; chatham (H2856), to seal.

expand to see more

Hebrew Bebay (H893) — Bebai; the head of a returning house.

Hebrew ben (H1121) — son; ‘the children of Bebai’ means his household.

Hebrew golah (H1473) — the captivity, the body of exiles.

Hebrew 'alah (H5927) — to go up; the word for going up to Jerusalem.

Hebrew chatham (H2856) — to seal; the covenant of Nehemiah 10.

Usage

"“The children of Bebai, six hundred twenty and three” — one household of the return."

"“Zechariah the son of Bebai, and with him twenty and eight males” — a later company."

"“Those that sealed were…” — the family bound by written covenant."
